review_notes: Independently read canonical gmmovieend.c lines 49-165 and gm_1A3F.c lines 149-362, and reconciled both input artifacts. Empty proposal is appropriate; inherited supported knowledge is retained without equivalent rewrites. Accept upstream deferrals: source declarations cannot establish compiled sections; literal xC/status behavior does not establish resetting identity; routing requests mode-state ID 0 rather than scene-kind 0. Acceptance is scoped to the empty change set and examined contradictions, not an independent re-audit of retained rows.

contradictions.reason: Accept deferral of the four compiled-layout facts and the .sdata2 link. Canonical declarations establish scalar and array types, filenames, and literal offsets, but do not establish section membership, section sizes, padding, constant-pool loads, or ordering. No compiled evidence supports promoting those claims.

Accept deferral of all six Movie End/reset-related facts. The pinned handler spells the field xC, not resetting. Its numeric status predicate has priority over simultaneous timeout or Start, and the invocation decrementing delay from one to zero still returns. The functionality document preserves these mechanics without treating rendered IsFinished naming as proof. The runner's resetting spelling alone does not establish equivalence to this handler's xC.

Accept deferral of both scene-routing links. Prize exit requests mode-state ID zero. The setter stores one, and the non-reset runner decodes and clears the request after exit processing. The broad routing association is plausible, but the frozen scene-index explanation should not be promoted as scene-kind selection.

unresolved: Compiled section placement, sizes, padding, and constant ordering remain deferred pending compiled evidence.
Canonical xC versus resetting identity and MTHP status polarity/progress units remain unresolved; rendered names are not proof.
The two baseline routing-link explanations remain deferred because mode-state routing is not scene-kind selection.
Shared gm_804D6724 clearing and movie teardown ownership require cross-file lifetime research; this TU assigns the callback, while the outer runner performs MTHP cleanup.
Inherited one-player and Zelda/Sheik context remains baseline interpretation rather than a newly independently verified upstream mapping.
